nodes.title: Canvas - 0.6 MP for 5s | 1.03 MP for 3s faces
MacMax - READ ME FIRST
widgets_values:
# MacMax - MiniMax H3 for Apple Silicon

*(MacMax = Mac + MiniMax. Any Apple Silicon Mac with enough unified memory. It is not a
Max-chip requirement.)*

Video with native stereo audio in one pass, running locally on a Mac. Smallest graph that
still does T2V / I2V / FLF, tuned to measured numbers rather than to the stock template's
defaults (which are presumably tuned for CUDA cards, where they may well be right).

**Memory:** the DiT is ~20 GB and the encoder ~15 GB, loaded in sequence. Tested at 48 GB.
32 GB is untested and expected to be tight; under 32 GB is not recommended. Reports from
other configurations welcome.

**Expect ~35 min** for the default 0.6 MP @ 5s / 20 steps, with Spectrum on as shipped
(~47 min if you bypass it).
**Step 1 takes several minutes on its own** because the text encoder loads first - it is not
hung. The seed widget ships on `randomize`; pin it to 6120072732051 to compare against our
numbers.

**New here? Read the green SETUP panel on the right first** (four model files, three custom
nodes, one launch flag). Then edit only the blue `1 - EDIT THESE` column and hit Run.

**Toggles.** Everything optional in this graph toggles the same way: select the node,
press **Ctrl+B** (bypass). Purple = off. No switch nodes, no extra packs.
- the two `LoadImage` nodes: both off = **T2V** (default), first on = **I2V**, both on = **FLF**
  (no R2V here - identity-from-reference-stills is a different conditioning node; use the
  Foxydit port that ships alongside)
- `Spectrum`: ships **ON** (-27%, faces hold). Bypass it for a pure uncached reference
- `EasyCache`: ships OFF and should stay off, see below. **Never run both at once**
- the `EXTRAS` column: audio preview (on), 1080x1920 export + audio stem (off)

**Troubleshooting.** Model loaders red on first load = your models sit in subfolders;
re-pick the four files once. That is the only expected error. If the GGUF loader is missing,
`pip install gguf==0.18.0` into the ComfyUI venv and restart with `ASFP8_INT8_EXT=1`.

**Why 0.6 MP @ 5s.** Cost is a **token budget**, not a resolution or a length limit:
tokens ~ megapixels x seconds. Measured, 20 steps:

| config | tokens | s/step | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.03 MP @ 3s | ~22k | 131.6 | comfortable |
| **0.6 MP @ 5s** | **~22k** | **137.8** | **near-identical cost, longer shots** |
| 1.03 MP @ 5s | ~37k | ~340 | ~3x wall clock, near the memory floor |

Those are sampling-only rates, uncached, so they are comparable to each other. Wall clock per
step is higher because it carries model load and decode.

**Spectrum ships ON, EasyCache ships OFF.** Both skip sampling steps, but not the same way,
and it shows. Same seed, same prompt, same 0.6 MP/5s canvas, measured on face crops resized
to a common size so resolution cannot win for free:

| | wall | fine detail | faces |
|---|---|---|---|
| uncached | 47:21 | 0.381 | reference |
| EasyCache 0.2 | 31:16 | **0.405** | mouths and teeth visibly smeared |
| **Spectrum d1** | **34:27** | 0.368 | **teeth and lips hold, no artefacts** |

Note EasyCache scores the **highest** on fine detail while looking the **worst**. It is not
resolving detail, it is injecting spurious high-frequency edge noise, so any sharpness metric
blesses it. This is the trap the earlier version of this pack fell into: it recommended
EasyCache on a 0.991 layout correlation computed on thumbnails that cannot see a mouth.

Spectrum *forecasts* the skipped steps from a fitted curve instead of reusing a cached state,
which is why fast-changing detail survives. Measured here: 8 of 20 steps forecast. It costs
~3 min more than EasyCache and is worth it on anything with a face. EasyCache stays in the
graph as a one-keypress option for faceless b-roll, where the artefacts have nothing to
damage. **Never enable both** - Spectrum's author is explicit about this.

**Steps: 20.** 15 and 20 show no measurable difference at this metric's resolution (0.940
both, vs the uncached 20-step reference) because they evaluate a similar number of real steps.
Below ~6 steps **speech breaks before video does** - at 4 steps
the picture is clean but dialogue loops or vanishes. Judge audio at 10+ steps only.

**Sigma shift** is stock 12/3. The Turbo LoRA workflow wants 12/6. I could not get that LoRA
to load on this machine (it OOMs at runtime regardless of canvas), but others report it
working, so treat that as my setup rather than a property of the model.

No triton, no SageAttention, nothing CUDA. None of it has an Apple Silicon build.

---
**MacMax** by MAD IT. Built on ComfyUI's shipped `video_minimax_h3_t2v` template - the graph
is that template flattened, so nothing here is a reimplementation. Numbers above are from
~40 measured renders on a single 48 GB M5 Pro; treat them as a strong prior, not a law.
One companion workflow for Apple Silicon ships alongside this one: a port of
**foxfuressence**'s filmmaking rig.

nodes.title: SETUP - models & custom nodes
widgets_values:
## Download these four files

Total ~41 GB. Paths are relative to your `ComfyUI/models/` folder.

**`diffusion_models/`**
- [minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/diffusion_models/minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors) - 20.9 GB

**`text_encoders/`**
- [qwen3vl-32B-MiniMax-H3-Q4_K_M.gguf](https://huggingface.co/realrebelai/MiniMax-H3_GGUFs/resolve/main/qwen3vl-32B-MiniMax-H3-Q4_K_M.gguf) - 14.6 GB
  ⚠ **GGUF, not the stock NVFP4-AWQ encoder** - that one is CUDA-only.

**`vae/`**
- [minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/vae/minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors) - 5.2 GB
- [minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/vae/minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors) - 0.6 GB

```
ComfyUI/models/
├── diffusion_models/minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors
├── text_encoders/qwen3vl-32B-MiniMax-H3-Q4_K_M.gguf
└── vae/minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors
    vae/minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors
```

### Custom nodes: exactly three
- **ComfyUI-GGUF** (city96), for the text encoder. Also `pip install gguf==0.18.0` or the
  node silently reports IMPORT FAILED.
- **ComfyUI-AppleSilicon-FP8**, required; the int8 path will not load without it.
- **ComfyUI-Spectrum-MiniMax-H3** (xmarre), **pinned to v0.2.3**. This graph ships with
  Spectrum ENABLED, so without it the `SpectrumApplyMiniMaxH3` node will not resolve and the
  workflow will not run. `install_node_packs.sh` pins it for you. If you would rather not add
  it, delete that node and reconnect sigma shift straight to the sampler: you lose 27% speed,
  nothing else.

`ResolutionSelector` is ComfyUI core (`comfy_extras/nodes_resolution.py`), not a custom
node. You do not need KJNodes or Resolution-Master for this workflow.

### Launch ComfyUI like this
```
ASFP8_INT8_EXT=1 python main.py --reserve-vram 10 --cache-none --disable-smart-memory
```
`ASFP8_INT8_EXT=1` is not optional. The memory flags matter because H3 loads three models
in sequence (encoder ~15 GB, DiT ~20 GB, VAEs ~6 GB) and never needs two at once.

### If the model loaders show red on first load
The workflow uses bare stock filenames. If you keep models in subfolders, click each loader
once and re-pick the file. That is the only expected error.

nodes.title: PROMPTING - read before your first render
widgets_values:
## Prompting H3 - the audio is half the model

H3 generates **video and stereo audio in one pass**. A one-line Stable-Diffusion-style
prompt will give you mediocre audio and you will conclude the model is overhyped. Give it
structure. This is the exact prompt used for every measurement in this pack:

```
Cinematic night footage, 35mm, shallow depth of field, wet tarmac, warm streetlight,
natural grain, no lettering anywhere in frame.

Scene overview: A white sedan rolls slowly along a wet European street at night.

Storyboard:
[0s-5s] One continuous take. The car moves steadily through frame as light travels
across the paint. No cuts.

Camera: Static low tracking shot at bumper height, slight handheld drift.

Audio: a deep V8 engine rolling past at low speed, tyres on wet tarmac, faint street
ambience.

Music: none

No text, subtitles, lettering, signage, logos or watermarks of any kind.
```

**Rules learned the hard way (measured over ~40 renders):**
- **ONE CONTINUOUS TAKE.** Writing "Shot 1 / Shot 2" makes H3 genuinely cut.
- **Name subjects specifically.** It anchors on the most specific noun phrase and fills the
  rest by association. "Large white American sedan" produced a 1960s classic; naming the
  exact model and its features produced the right car every time. **Partial specificity is
  worse than none** - it looks like it worked.
- **Speech must be written out verbatim** or you get gibberish. And judge audio only at
  10+ steps: below ~6 steps speech breaks before the picture does.
- **Setting gets overridden** more readily than subject, lighting or camera. If a location
  is non-negotiable, lead with it.
- **Negatives about CONTENT are unreliable** ("no visible faces" was ignored repeatedly).
  Negatives about *lettering* do hold.

Frame count: duration is snapped by the maths node to the model's grid - frames must satisfy
`n % 17 == 5`, so 5.0s becomes 124 frames, not 120. That is why the expression looks odd.

nodes.title: PROMPT + conditioning
widgets_values:
Vertical smartphone-style portrait video, 28mm front camera look, soft late-afternoon window light from the left, natural skin texture, slight handheld drift, fine grain, no lettering anywhere in frame.

Scene overview: A woman in her late twenties stands in a bright home kitchen talking straight to camera, casual and warm, like a phone recording.

Storyboard:
[0s-5s] Shot 1: Vertical medium close-up, head and shoulders filling the upper two thirds of the frame, kitchen counter and a window softly out of focus behind her. She looks into the lens and speaks, one small nod, natural blink.

Camera: Static Shot held at chest height, very slight handheld drift.

Audio: her voice, close and clear with a natural American accent, faint room tone and a distant street hum underneath. She says: "This whole clip came out of a laptop. Picture and sound, one pass, no studio."

Music: none

No text, subtitles, lettering, signage, logos or watermarks of any kind.

nodes.title: EasyCache OFF - smears faces. Spectrum is on instead, never run both

widgets_values:
## CHAINING (Motion Context) + LOW-RAM TEXT ENCODER

**Chain clips (motion + audio continue across the cut).** Needs
[ComfyUI-H3-Motion-Context](https://github.com/NikoDemon80/ComfyUI-H3-Motion-Context).
All four nodes here ship BYPASSED. Before rendering a clip you may want to continue,
un-bypass Save Latent (~7 MB per clip under output/h3_context/) - a clip rendered without
it cannot be continued later. To CONTINUE a clip: un-bypass Motion Context, Trim and
Load Latent as well, set Load Latent clip_index to the clip you continue FROM and Save
Latent clip_index to the clip this one IS, queue. The continuation comes back exactly 22
frames shorter (the pinned context, trimmed for clean concat). Validated on a 48GB M5:
5s + 5s join r=0.95, the audio bed continues (small level swell). Resolution must match
between chained clips. Motion Context refuses to run without a context latent wired.

**Low-RAM text encoder (optional).** The bypassed ClipProj Loader swaps the 13.6 GB 32B
GGUF encoder for Qwen3-VL-8B fp8 (+380 MB projection) ~= 3.7 GB lighter - this is what
makes 5s takes fit in 48 GB. Needs
[ComfyUI-ClipProj](https://github.com/nicolab28/ComfyUI-ClipProj) + matrices from
HF NicoLab28/ClipProj-MiniMax-H3. To use: un-bypass and wire its CLIP output in place of
the GGUF loader. Seed-matched A/B vs GGUF: identity, wardrobe and spoken lines held;
speed unchanged. Prompt-sensitive edge cases exist (proper nouns) - eyeball outputs.
